title: Arch Manning remains Texas starting QB: Steve Sarkisian says he needs 'better version' of star - CBS Sports
description: The Longhorns coach went long on his team's quarterback situation entering Saturday's game against Ole Miss
body:
The Longhorns coach went long on his team's quarterback situation entering Saturday's game against Ole Miss
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 19, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:26 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Texas coach Steve Sarkisian is sticking with Arch Manning as his starting quarterback ahead of Saturday's showdown with seventh-ranked Ole Miss, but he acknowledged the leash on the former five-star could be shortened this season."Arch can play better for us; he's our starter, but I need to see a better version of Arch Manning," Sarkisian said Monday. "Like I need to see a better version of a lot of guys on our offensive football team right now. We need to see a better version of him this week."After previous reports of backup KJ Lacey seeing an "uptick" in first-team reps in practice this week after Manning's struggles over the weekend against Florida, Sarkisian said Lacey takes first-team reps every week.Sarkisian said after Saturday's 27-24 loss to the Gators that "everything" would be evaluated throughout his program following the Longhorns' recent two-game skid that torched their top-10 ranking.
This comes after Sarkisian defended Manning after his two-interception, fourth-quarter performance during a loss to Oklahoma this month and said his quarterback always receives unfair criticism.The tune has changed a bit after Manning lost his first career home game over the weekend thanks to a costly late-game fumble."I just felt like we didn't play good offensive football, and we're not playing great offensive football right now," Sarkisian said.
Manning has regressed this season from a consistency standpoint when compared to the final six starts of the 2025 campaign, his first as a starter. Manning has thrown for 1,295 yards, 11 touchdowns and five interceptions this season, four of those giveaways coming against Power Four competition.The attention to Manning seems to have played a part in the Longhorns' lack of cohesion offensively, from execution to play-calling from Sarkisian. Texas ranks 12th in the SEC in total offense after seven games, 13th in rushing offense and 15th in explosive plays — stunning numbers when you consider the overall talent on the Longhorns' roster.He hasn't been on the same page with his receivers and several times last time out left passes short of his intended targets and was nearly picked off, including a long ball to Cam Coleman.
Sarkisian put the blame on his quarterback following the late-game fumble."I think on that play, our protection might've been OK," Sarkisian said. "I think [Manning] might have been a little quick to kind of drop his eyes. He had Emmett Mosley, who's the primary [receiver]. We thought the ball could have got out."Manning's response to his coach's evaluation remarks was swift and honest."Yeah, I mean everyone's evaluated every week. That's how it is when you go to a school like this with elite players. Everyone's gotta get better, and that starts with me," he said after Saturday's loss.Who is K.J. Lacey?A 2025 signee for the Longhorns, Lacey was one of two quarterbacks Sarkisian offered during that recruiting cycle — the other was Bryce Underwood (Michigan). An Alabama native, Lacey won a 6A state title at Saraland as a four-star prospect and has made three career appearances over his first two seasons with the Longhorns.
Lacey is the No. 2 passer in Alabama prep football history with 10,985 yards. He completed five of his seven attempts for 55 yards in the season opener against Texas State and went 1-for-1 for 8 yards earlier this fall against UTSA. Sarkisian acknowledged Monday that Lacey's split reps haven't changed this season behind Manning but pointed out "we'll find out as the week goes."Texas leads the SEC in three-and-out rate and has not been able to push the opposition off the football in the run game despite the offseason acquisitions of Hollywood Smothers (NC State) and Raleek Brown (Arizona State). Like Manning, Lacey can make plays with his legs, but remains a pocket-first passer.

title: Why Eagles won't tank after Jalen Hurts injury: NFC East race, trade deadline outlook - CBS Sports
description: The Eagles have little reason to intentionally tank, but an upcoming three-game divisional stretch will reveal wh
body:
The Eagles have little reason to intentionally tank, but an upcoming three-game divisional stretch will reveal whether they can salvage their season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 19, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:55 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Philadelphia Eagles' season was already seemingly falling apart before the team boarded a plane to London. With two more losses since then, along with Monday's news that Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season, the narrative that the Eagles are in freefall is in full effect. In any other situation, the Eagles would embark on an organic tank, a byproduct of the team's mounting injuries and losses. Losing is never acceptable (especially in a city like Philadelphia, which prides itself on overcoming the odds), but it would be understood, given the amount of body blows the Eagles have already endured. The Eagles won't intentionally tank, however. There's too much football left to play, the Eagles have too many good players on their roster, and they play in the NFL's easiest division to win. Philadelphia's objective, at least to me, is clear: win as many games as you can with the players you have. Best case, the Eagles find a way to win a division that could be had with seven wins. Worst case, the Eagles stumble into a top-five pick in next year's draft. 
Before we look ahead, let's look back at the Eagles' first six games. Four of their first five games were one-score outcomes (the only outlier was the embarrassing loss in Chicago in Week 3). On Sunday, the Eagles weren't put away until Bryce Young's second touchdown pass made it an 11-point game with 6:33 left. Philadelphia gave the defending NFC South champs a fight despite the absence of Hurts and Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and losing Nolan Smith during the game (concussion). In a losing effort, the Eagles received encouraging performances from DeVonta Smith (75 yards and a touchdown), Dallas Goedert (six catches for 61 yards in his second game back from injury), linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr. (six tackles and a half-sack) and defensive end Arnold Ebiketie (nine tackles). Sunday was essentially Tanner McKee's first legitimate start (his first two starts the previous two seasons were in meaningless games where the vast majority of the starters rested). Given the circumstances, McKee's performance wasn't bad by any stretch. He attempted 45 passes (way too many for a player in his position), completed 26, and threw for 215 yards and a touchdown. His stat line did not include an interception, which is impressive given his lack of experience and the number of times he threw the ball up. 
McKee's performance is even more impressive when you factor in that he was sacked 3 times and had no running game to take the pressure off him. 
The Eagles' next three games will likely determine how the rest of the season plays out. Each game is against NFC East division foes, with two of the games being played in Philadelphia. Philadelphia hosts Dallas this weekend, travels to Washington in Week 8, hosts the Giants in Week 9, and then heads into its bye week. The Eagles are in second place in the NFC East, 1.5 games behind first-place New York. If the Eagles can win two of their upcoming three games (including the matchup with the Giants), they will still be in the hunt to win the division entering Week 11, when Philadelphia will host a Steelers team that hasn't won in the City of Brotherly Love since 1965. 
The Eagles' next three games will determine how GM Howie Roseman handles the trade deadline, which falls during Philadelphia's bye week. If the Eagles show signs of revival during that span, Roseman may try to acquire a few players who can help them win a weak division. Roseman won't do anything that will mortgage the team's future, however. The more likely scenario is Roseman either standing pat or dealing a few pricey veterans to teams hoping to make a playoff push. Roseman would surely like to add to his pile of future draft picks that includes a projected eight picks in 2027 and two first- and two second-round picks in 2028. As bleak as it looks, the Eagles can win the NFC East if they right the ship during the next three weeks. Crazier things have happened, like in 2017, when the Eagles defeated Tom Brady and the Patriots in the Super Bowl with backup quarterback Nick Foles winning MVP honors. 
If the Eagles can't turn things around in the next three weeks, Roseman can start making moves to improve his team's situation in 2027 and beyond.

        Every week matters in the 2026 NWSL regular season, even as the year heads into the final stretch. With just two matches remaining, players are still finding ways to leave their mark on games. That means it's time to give out Attacking Third Team of the Week honors.After weekly matches across the 2026 NWSL season, Attacking Third analysts will select players, a head coach, and an honorary captain based on weekend performances. With the longest season in NWSL history, a 30-match schedule per team, selecting 11 players each week is never easy. Here you can find a mix of stats and data, analysis from our pundits, and highlights you may have missed over the weekend. If you're keeping track of who earned past honors, check out our previous team of the week.Here's who made the latest edition:Goalkeeper: Sandra Paños (San Diego Wave FC)San Diego Wave is in standout form with the playoffs ahead, and part of that is because they've cemented their goalkeeper position. The club settled on a crucial position after rotating Luisa Agudelo, Leah Freeman, and Didi Haracic, bringing in Sandra Paños midseason from Club América. She faced 23 crosses and 13 shots, and made three saves against North Carolina for another standout performance and three more points in the NWSL Shield race.
Defender: Sofia Huerta (Seattle Reign FC)When your team is hovering just under the playoff line, every game is a must-win. Outside back Sofia Huerta added to her all-time assist record (35) by setting up an insurance goal for Nerilia Mondesir. 
Defender: Gabrielle Robinson (Kansas City Current)The Kansas City Current are surging at the right time, and that includes underrated backline efforts. This week, Gabrielle Robinson gets the honors for a reliable shift at centerback, where she led the team in clearances (five) and co-led in interceptions (two), helping the team earn a clean sheet against Utah Royals.Defender: Mimi Van Zanten (San Diego Wave FC)Welcome back to the team of the week, Mimi Van Zanten. The rookie outside back has racked up consistent starts all season, and her shift over the weekend against North Carolina was no exception. Whether it's getting more involved up the pitch in attack or tracking back in recovery, Van Zanten stands out. She led the team in tackles (six) and the backline in recoveries (seven).
Defender: Gabrielle Carle (Washington Spirit)Washington Spirit's Gabrielle Carle made a massive impact in a heavyweight battle against Gotham FC over the weekend. She helped keep a clean sheet and led the team in touches (62), tackles (five), and duels (11). The win clinched a playoff spot for the Spirit and keeps them in contention for the NWSL Shield.Midfielder: Melissa Bethi (Washington Spirit)Algerian international midfielder Melissa Bethi was a game-changer in the second half of an important game with playoff implications. She delivered the game-winning assist to Lucia Di Guglielmo.
Midfielder: Ally Sentnor (Angel City FC)If there's a goal from distance, there's a chance that Ally Sentnor is behind it. Over the weekend, she delivered a dagger into Denver Summit's playoff hopes with a game-winning goal.
Midfielder: Kenza Dali (San Diego Wave FC)San Diego Wave FC midfielder Kenza Dali is a glue player for the team this year. The Wave are far better with her on the pitch than without, and her efforts to build up play on Melanie Barcenas' goal are why she is such an important player. 
Forward: Maddie Mercado (Seattle Reign FC)Three big points are easy to get when Seattle Reign's Maddie Mercado steps onto the pitch and scores two goals. Her clinical finish on a long lob from Jess Fishlock earns her a spot on the team of the week. 
Forward: Haley Hopkins (Kansas City Current)There might not be a player more clutch for her team than Haley Hopkins is for the Kansas City Current. She's scored six goals in three games, including a brace against Utah Royals over the weekend.
Forward: Trinity Byars (San Diego Wave FC)San Diego aren't just putting the ball in the back of the net; they're scoring beautiful goals, from Melanie Barcenas' rocket to Trinity Byars' crafty game-winning chip. 
Coach: Adrian Gonzalez (Washington Spirit)With a win that clinched a playoff spot and kept Washington Spirit alive in the NWSL Shield race, coach of the week honors go to Adrian Gonzalez. A spectacularly executed game plan to stay compact against Gotham, manage minutes for Leicy Santos' return, and adjust with a sub for Bethi is just icing on the cake.Honorary captain: Lucia Di Guglielmo (Washington Spirit)Congratulations to Lucia Di Guglielmo on nabbing the game-winner and scoring her first-ever NWSL goal. The Italian international joined the Spirit in the offseason.

title: College basketball rankings: Florida earns No. 1 spot in preseason AP Top 25 poll ahead of Duke, Illinois - CBS Sports
description: The Gators are the preseason No. 1 team in the AP Top 25 poll for the first time since 2006.
body:
The Gators are the preseason No. 1 team in the AP Top 25 poll for the first time since 2006.
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 19, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:05 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Florida is ranked No. 1 in the preseason AP Top 25 men's basketball poll released Monday after earning 47 of a possible 59 first-place votes. It marks the first time since 2006 that the Gators will open the college basketball campaign as the preseason top-ranked team.The Gators were widely expected to begin the season No. 1 after a key offseason of retention that saw Todd Golden's squad return four starters (Thomas Haugh, Rueben Chinyelu, Alex Condon and Boogie Fland) from a team that won 27 games during the 2025-26 season and earned a No. 1 seed in the NCAA Tournament for the second consecutive season.The last time Florida debuted at No. 1 in the preseason poll was when the program was coming off its first national title and returned a nucleus of its team, including Corey Brewer, Al Horford, Joakim Noah and Taurean Green. Florida went on to win its second consecutive title after opening the season at No. 1Florida remains one of two programs — with UConn being the other — to win back-to-back national titles this century. The Gators will have an opportunity to make it two championships in three seasons if Florida is the final team standing in Detroit come April.

        
            
                Trey Kaufman-Renn signs with Kansas: Former Purdue star is seeking unprecedented sixth year of eligibility
                
                    Cameron Salerno                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
While Florida was penciled in at No. 1 the last several weeks, Duke earning the No. 2 spot was also expected. The Blue Devils return Dame Sarr, Cayden Boozer, Caleb Foster and Patrick Ngongba II from last year's team that earned the No. 1 overall seed in the NCAA Tournament. In addition to those returners, Duke welcomes in a star-studded high school recruiting class headlined by big man Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje — the projected No. 1 overall pick in the 2028 NBA Draft — and Wisconsin transfer John Blackwell, who earned preseason second-team All-American honors by CBS Sports.Illinois opens the season ranked No. 3. The Fighting Illini reached the Final Four for the first time since 2005 and will be led by preseason first-team All-American forward David Mirković. UConn — the team that ended Illinois' season  (UConn) in Indianapolis earlier this spring— debuts at No. 4 in the poll.Florida, Duke and Illinois were the lone teams to receive first-place votes in the poll.

Purdue opened the season ranked No. 1 in 2025-26 but received only 35 first-place votes. Houston (16), Florida (8) and UConn (2) all received at least one first-place vote.  Ahead of the 2026-27 season, AP voters are more aligned on who is the top team in college basketball. Only three teams received first-place votes, with Duke and Illinois combining to receive 12 of them. Florida received 47 first-place votes, which is high for the season's first poll. The Gators will be tested early and often this season. On opening night, Florida has a date with in-state foe Miami (ranked No. 14) in Tampa to open the 2026-27 season. That game will be a major measuring stick for both programs.

        
            
                SEC Media Days Takeaways: Florida's Rueben Chinyelu guarantees national title, LSU litigation saga continues
                
                    Matt Norlander                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Kansas and Texas Tech ranked in teens due to roster questionsOn paper, Kansas and Texas Tech have very good rosters that you could argue are both top 10 in the sport. However, voters appear to be taking a cautious approach, with both teams ahead of this season due to each having three players in eligibility limbo. For Texas Tech, that would be Donovan Atwell, Darrion Williams and Jamichael Stillwell. As for Kansas, Trey Kaufman-Renn, who signed with the program hours before the first poll of the season was announced, is looking to become eligible alongside Tre White and Melvin Council Jr.Those are the two teams, plus Houston, that are expected to challenge Arizona for the Big 12 titles this season.Reigning champs open at No. 16After putting together one of the most dominant NCAA Tournament runs of the modern era earlier this year, Michigan will open the season ranked No. 16. The Wolverines are in the midst of massive turnover after saying goodbye to four starters and head coach Dusty May from their national title team. In addition to those departures, five-star guard Brandon McCoy Jr. — who was expected to start and play a significant role for Michigan this season — won't play after suffering a torn ACL earlier this summer.
Preseason All-American guard Elliot Cadeau is the lone starter from Michigan's title team returning, but the outlook could change if Roddy Gayle Jr. — a key reserve from last year's squad — is granted a fifth year. Trey McKenney, another key reserve from last season's title team, should be one of the top breakout candidates in college basketball to monitor who could make Michigan a contender.

        Another UEFA Champions League week is upon us, and what a week it's already shaping up to be. The Eagles quarterback is clinically stable and expected to make a full recovery, but he cannot participate in contact activities

        Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season, according to multiple reports, after blood clots were found in his lungs. The Eagles and Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, issued a joint statement on Monday laying out his updated diagnosis after originally announcing he had a superficial blood clot in his left calf that caused him to miss Week 6. A follow-up scan over the weekend revealed deep vein thrombosis, and he had "bilateral pulmonary emboli," meaning several blood clots were now in his lungs.The Eagles said Hurts' prognosis is "very good" and that he is expected to make a full recovery. However, he will be treated with blood thinners, which will take him away from football activities until he is off the treatment.Here is the full statement:"Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition."Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e. "blood thinners"). During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football."Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects."We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery."No clots were found until Hurts was in London. It was initially diagnosed as a superficial blood clot. At that time, doctors advised Hurts not to sleep as a precaution, so he stayed awake for roughly 36 hours prior to the game against the Jaguars, according to reports. Despite not getting any sleep, Hurts started and threw for 220 yards and a touchdown. 
It was since discovered that the blood clot was "provoked," meaning that it was caused by Hurts getting cleated in his calf during the Eagles' Week 4 loss to the Rams. That game took place a week before Philadelphia's game in London. Hurts traveled to London that week, appearing on that week's injury report with a calf injury on Friday. He was a full practice participant that day and had no injury designation prior to the Eagles' game against the Jaguars. Hurts reportedly went to the hospital the evening prior to Sunday's game. Philadelphia will move forward with Tanner McKee at quarterback. A 2023 sixth-round pick, McKee made his first start of the season Sunday against the Panthers. He threw for 215 yards and a touchdown in a 25-15 loss that dropped the Eagles to 2-4.   Hurts, 28, is in his seventh season with the Eagles, who selected him in the second round of the 2020 NFL Draft. During his first six seasons, Hurts earned three Pro Bowl selections and helped lead the Eagles to two NFC titles and a Super Bowl title at the end of the 2024 season. He holds the single-game Super Bowl record for rushing yards by a quarterback (72 against the Chiefs). Hurts is one of just two players (the other being Terrell Davis) to run for three touchdowns in a Super Bowl game. 
Hurts was named MVP of Super Bowl LIX after amassing 293 total yards and scoring three total touchdowns in the Eagles' 40-22 win over the Chiefs. Hurts has the highest career completion percentage (73.3%) in Super Bowl history among passers with at least 40 attempts.

Ballard's exit raises questions about the direction of the Colts' franchise

        The Indianapolis Colts are in search of a new general manager. The franchise announced that it fired Chris Ballard following its 2-4 start to the season and back-to-back losses, the most recent of which came against the previously winless Tennessee Titans.Ballard had been under pressure since the second half of last season, when the Colts lost seven consecutive games and eight of their final nine to close the year. Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon, when she made the decision to retain Ballard and the coaching staff after that disappointing finish, set the expectation that improvement must come in 2026."I am grateful to Chris for his years of service to the Colts and for everything he poured into this organization," Irsay-Gordon said in a statement. "He cared deeply about our team and our community, and we wish Chris and his family all the best. As I said at the start of the season, the sense of urgency has never been higher. Our standard is to compete for championships, and I believe a change in leadership is necessary to meet that standard."
This season was Ballard's 10th as the general manager. Under his watch, the Colts posted a 72-82-1 record and were 1-2 in the postseason. Time ran out on his tenure following five consecutive years without a playoff appearance, which placed Indianapolis in a tie for the third-longest active drought in the NFL. Only the Atlanta Falcons (2017) and New York Jets (2010) have waited longer for a return to the playoffs.
What's more, the Colts were the only team in the AFC South to fail to win the division during Ballard's tenure. Each of the other franchises won it at least twice."Making the change during the season was a deliberate decision," Irsay-Gordon said. "Waiting would only delay the important work that needs to begin now. We will conduct a thorough search for our next general manager and take the time necessary to identify the right leader for the future of the organization. I also want to be clear: this decision does not change our goals for the season. We have a lot of football in front of us, and I expect us to compete, improve, and win football games."Ballard was in the final year of his contract and said before the start of Year 10 that he would not sign an extension prior to the start of the season. Irsay-Gordon's comments about his retention after 2025 indicated that he would have had to deliver a bounce-back season to earn another contract.
Pressure mounts on Shane SteichenThe first domino has fallen in Indianapolis, and it is now on Shane Steichen to prevent a chain reaction. The fourth-year coach entered the season on the same kind of hot seat as Ballard, because Irsay-Gordon said that he, too, understood the sense of urgency had never been higher. With one man fired, the focus now shifts to the other. Barring an in-season turnaround, Steichen could soon find the same fate.Steichen can only operate with the players presented to him, and that Ballard was the first to go shows the Colts' issues go deeper than the coaching staff. There are clear roster deficiencies that limit the team's potential. At the same time, though, successful coaches make the most of what they have at their disposal, and Steichen is missing the opportunity to do so. The 2-4 start to the season puts Steichen on pace for the worst year of his tenure. With watchful eyes scrutinizing his every move, the team seems to have regressed.Boos rained down from the stands inside Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday during the 26-20 loss to the Titans. Steichen said after the game that he does not blame fans for booing "one freaking bit." While some change is clearly necessary, Steichen committed on Daniel Jones as the team's starting quarterback and said, "We've got a lot to fix, and we've got to fix it in a hurry."
Sauce Gardner trade among Chris Ballard's most head-scratching movesWhen the Colts opened the 2025 season at 7-1, Ballard decided to push all of his chips forward and trade future capital for an asset that could help the team capitalize on its hot start. The move backfired. Ballard gave up two first-round picks and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell for cornerback Sauce Gardner, and neither side of the deal worked in his favor. Gardner has struggled during his time in Indianapolis, while the New York Jets cashed in by constructing a young and promising offensive core with its newfound assets.While that was the most glaring single failure of Ballard's tenure, his missteps primarily occurred at the quarterback position and in succession, putting the Colts in a hole they could not climb out of. In the years since Andrew Luck's retirement, Ballard was unable to find a long-term solution at the position. Only two quarterbacks started consecutive season openers, and neither of them has made it to the playoffs.
Colts' Week 1 starting quarterbacks since Andrew Luck's retirementJacoby Brissett (2019)Philip Rivers (2020)Carson Wentz (2021)Matt Ryan (2022)Anthony Richardson (2023, 2024)Daniel Jones (2025, 2026)During that stretch, the Colts used a first-round pick on Richardson, who did not amount to anything more than a backup. They also gave Jones a two-year, $88 million contract extension in March despite the fact that he tore his Achilles last season. Those investments aged poorly, as did many of Ballard's moves in the latter stages of his tenure.

body:
A cardiologist weighs in on how Hurts' condition contrasts with DVTs, standard treatment methods and what could determine the recovery timeline
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 19, 2026

    12:28 pm ET

            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Editor's Note: This article was originally published on Oct. 17 after Jalen Hurts was diagnosed with a superficial blood clot. The Eagles have since announced that Hurts now has deep vein thrombosis, and multiple blood clots were found in his lungs. He is now expected to miss the remainder of the season.Jalen Hurts' 2026 season was put on pause this week, as the Philadelphia Eagles quarterback was diagnosed with a superficial blood clot that had experienced some movement and the team placed him on IR on Saturday.The team diagnosed the clot and informed the league of Hurts' situation last week, but he was cleared to suit up and play in their Week 5 London loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. After a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the clot, the team announced that Hurts would have to sit out for at least one week while they treated him. It initially looked like the quarterback would avoid injured reserve, but ESPN reported Saturday afternoon that after consultations with doctors and experts, the Eagles decided to place Hurts on injured reserve -- meaning he will miss at least the next four games. What is a superficial blood clot and how much time could Hurts miss? CBS Sports spoke to Dr. Henry Han at UT Southwestern to get some answers. Dr. Han is a board certified cardiologist that works at the intersection of cardiology and vascular medicine. He has seen clot-related diseases, diseases related to aneurysms, tears in blood vessels, and is very familiar with superficial vein thrombosis.
What exactly is Jalen Hurts dealing with?A superficial blood clot could be classified as "superficial thrombophlebitis," or a much easier term: "superficial vein thrombosis." Dr. Han: "Basically it's a blood clot that's in one of the veins that's on the surface level underneath the skin. We typically find it in the leg, sometimes we find it in the arm. What happens is when the clot forms there, the vein gets inflamed. And so the area turns really red, it gets warm and it gets tender."What's the difference between a superficial clot and the 'deep vein thrombosis' (DVT) that we've seen in sports? This is a situation that deserves monitoring, but it's also not the more serious "deep vein thrombosis" we've seen in sports before. Spurs superstar Victor Wembanyama, for example, was forced to miss the final 30 games of the 2024-25 season after doctors discovered deep vein thrombosis in his right shoulder. Then there's two-time NBA champion Chris Bosh, who was forced to retire early due to a clotting condition. 
Dr. Han: "Superficial clots that sit near the surface on your surface veins are a lot less dangerous compared to the DVT (deep vein thrombosis). In sports we hear about the DVTs that for some athletes end up being sort of career-enders. The interesting part is that the superficial vein thromboses typically are not dangerous to that degree and the treatment for what you would need for both is a little bit different as well."What exactly caused this?In their statement released on Thursday, the Eagles said that four days after the Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, Hurts requested treatment on his calf. He believed he was kicked or cleated in the game.It's true that trauma to the area could have caused this clot, but we simply don't have enough information to say that definitively. 
Dr. Han: "I can't speak to the exact specific case, but sort of generalities, anything that irritates a vein or slows the blood flow can trigger it. So we actually see this for people who have gotten IVs or blood draws when you have a needle in the vein that causes the irritation and damage. Other things too, like long flights. We know that certain hormone medications, pregnancy for women. But definitely trauma is one of the major causes that can cause this sort of superficial thrombophlebitis."What are the treatment options?There are numerous cases of NFL players missing time due to blood clots. Take Carolina Panthers star right tackle Taylor Moton for example, who hasn't played at all this season because doctors found blood clots in his lung this summer. That situation required Moton to immediately be placed on blood thinners. Moton having blood clots found in one of his lungs is a much more serious situation than superficial thrombophlebitis. It varies case to case, of course, but treatments for what Hurts has been diagnosed with can sometimes be simple. 
Dr. Han: "Usually what we end up doing for standard of care is that within the first week, you can actually for a lot of patients and a lot of people, you can actually do conservative treatment, which involves things like anti-inflammatory medications, things like ibuprofen or naproxen, staying active, keeping the leg elevated, compression as sort of the first line. "In these kinds of situations, we actually often think that the superficial thrombophlebitis is a self-contained issue. Usually what I do for my patients is that we do a follow-up scan either 7 or 14 days after the fact.  And if we see that the quality of the clot has changed, whether the clot is extended or it has moved or we do find it in deeper veins, then that kind of changes the equation for being more aggressive with treatments, which would include things as we typically do for deep vein thrombosis, the DVTs. That would be the full-on blood thinners, anticoagulants." So, could Hurts require blood thinners? Dr. Han: "If it's for superficial thrombophlebitis, not every case needs to be treated with blood thinners. The cases that I treat with blood thinners are for patients that are have the clots that are getting longer or building up, so to speak, or if the patients are profoundly symptomatic with lots of pain that ibuprofen and warm compresses and elevating legs and wearing a compression garment is not cutting it. For those patients, then we do often think about reaching towards anticoagulants, blood thinners. Although the period for treatment for superficial thrombophlebitis is actually much shorter than what we would treat for DVTs. The treatment here is usually a month and a half, 45 days of treatment is sufficient, whereas the DVT sometimes is lifelong, sometimes it's between three to six months."
When could Hurts return?Everyone wants to know: when could the Eagles quarterback return to the field? Since this is not a worst-case scenario like deep vein thrombosis, we asked Dr. Han before Hurts was placed on injured reserve if there was any chance he could miss just one or two weeksTwo key factors are whether he requires blood thinners and whether this clot is indeed a self-contained issue.Dr. Han: "It is possible. Again, just because I don't know the details of the case. The risk as I see it is being on a blood thinner and playing a contact sport would put him at extremely high risk of bleeding. And that's all bleeding complications -- blood trauma, but also internal bleeding. Oftentimes for athletics to this degree, it becomes a very strong safety consideration for being able to play or not. It's also a little hard for me to speculate if their phrasing for it -- 'It's moving' -- means that there are clots in other places, then the timeline for when he might come back is a lot harder for me to say.
"I would say the standard is if he was on blood thinners for just superficial thrombophlebitis that could be -- for symptomatic treatment -- that could be upwards of 45 days for treatment. But if there are extenuating circumstances that would have progressed or made it more dangerous or had turned into a deep vein thrombosis or something like that, then the treatment times could be much longer."

title: Pick Six: Jalen Hurts could be done for the year, plus Colts fire GM Chris Ballard and Commanders-49ers picks - CBS Sports

body:
Hello football friends, and welcome to the Monday edition of the Pick Six newsletter!It's not even Halloween yet, and we already have our first firing of the season. The Colts decided to dump general manager Chris Ballard on Monday in a move that came less than 24 hours after a loss to the 0-5 Titans. When you lose to a winless team, heads are going to roll. Ballard's was the first, but it might not be the last. Colts owner Carli Irsay-Gordon certainly sent a message to the organization by dumping Ballard, who has been the team's general manager since 2017. If you want all the details on the firing, be sure to read our full story here. I'll wait here while you guys read. Alright, now, let's move on to today's newsletter. We've got our standard Monday stuff plus a big update on the health of Jalen Hurts. 
As always, here's your daily reminder to tell all your friends to sign up for the newsletter. To get them signed up, just click here.  1. Jalen Hurts likely out for the season: Three things to know about QB's surprise injury
                                                                    Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images
                                                            Jalen Hurts is likely going to miss the rest of the season after blood clots were discovered in his lungs over the weekend. The Eagles quarterback is now taking blood thinners, and he's expected to make a full recovery, but while he's on the blood thinners, he's not allowed to take part in any contact activity, including football. Due to blood thinners, Hurts is expected to miss "multiple months," according to Tom Pelissero, and if that timeline holds, it would sideline him for the rest of the season. Here's everything you need to know about the situation: How the injury happened. Hurts' injury nightmare actually started in Week 4 against the Rams when he got cleated in the leg. That injury eventually escalated into a superficial vein thrombosis, which he was diagnosed with while in London getting ready for the Eagles' Week 5 game against the Jaguars. Hurts wasn't allowed to sleep before the Jaguars game. After doctors in London discovered the clot, Hurts had to stay in the hospital until 4 a.m. the night before the Jags' game. He also wasn't allowed to sleep the night before the game, because doctors viewed sleep as a risk, according to NFL Network. By the time the game kicked off, Hurts had been awake for almost 36 hours. The new diagnosis. After the Eagles got back to the United States, Hurts continued to undergo tests. According to his agent Nicole Lynn, the latest diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. Basically, the clots traveled from his calf to his lung. The Eagles placed Hurts on injured reserve over the weekend. With Hurts now likely out for the season, the Eagles will have an interesting decision to make. They could have a fire sale and start trading players away in an effort to build next year, or they could go out and acquire a quarterback and try to win the NFC East this year. That second option might sound crazy, but the NFC East is the worst division in football, and the Eagles are still very much in the race. 
If you want the full story on Hurts' injury, we've got that here. 


    2. NFL Week 6 grades: Browns are in first place in AFC NorthI never thought we'd live in a world where the Browns are in first place this late in the season, but here we are. After beating the Ravens on Sunday, the Browns are in first place after Week 6 for the first time in 12 years. That was Johnny Manziel's rookie year, and not much has gone right for the Browns since then. Anyway, we have some grades to hand out, and we're going to start off with Cleveland's win over Baltimore. Browns 13-10 over RavensRavens takeaway: When you don't have Lamar Jackson, you have to play nearly perfect football to win, and the Ravens simply didn't do that here. Baltimore essentially gave this game away in the fourth quarter with a missed field goal by Tyler Loop and a fumble by Derrick Henry on back-to-back possessions. The fumble set up a short TD drive for Cleveland, tying the game at 10. The Ravens' defense also struggled in the fourth quarter. Baltimore held Cleveland to just 237 yards of offense for the game, but 130 of that came in the final quarter. The problem for the Ravens is that this was another blown fourth-quarter lead. The blown leads were one reason why John Harbaugh got fired, and Jesse Minter hasn't quite figured out how to fix the problem. Going 1-1 without Lamar Jackson isn't the worst thing, but the Ravens were a few mistakes away from going 2-0 without their starting QB, and they'll certainly kick themselves for this divisional loss. Grade: B-Browns takeaway: If you've seen one Browns game this season, you've seen them all: Cleveland's defense keeps the game close until the fourth quarter, and then the offense wins it with a miracle drive. And that's exactly what happened here. After surrendering 10 quick points in the first quarter, the Browns only gave up 123 yards over the final three quarters combined. Not even Derrick Henry could get going against this defense. In the fourth quarter, Deshaun Watson took over. He only threw for 164 yards in this game, but 94 of that came in the final quarter. Jerry Jeudy, who's been an afterthought this year, had his biggest game of the season with four catches for 69 yards, including a 33-yard catch that helped set up Andre Szmyt. The miracle Browns might be for real. Grade: B+Texans 34-31 over JaguarsTexans takeaway: After taking a small step back in each of the past two years, C.J. Stroud looks like a quarterback who's finally ready to take a huge step forward. With the Texans' defense struggling, the offense has had to carry the load this year, and Stroud was certainly up to the task in his game, throwing for 312 yards and three touchdowns. The Texans have been looking for a No. 2 receiver behind Nico Collins, and they might have found one in Jaylin Noel, who had a monster game (four catches for 107 yards). And let's not forget about Marvin Harrison Jr. In his first game with the Texans, he looked completely comfortable out there while catching passes from his former college QB (Harrison caught three passes for 34 yards). The biggest question mark with the Texans right now is with their defense, and if that unit starts to play like it did last year, then Houston is likely going to march right back into the AFC South race after starting the season 0-4. Grade: BJaguars takeaway: Travis Hunter has officially arrived. Yes, the Jags lost this game, but if there was one upside, it was Hunter. He played his most offensive snaps of the season, and it paid off on a day when he caught four passes for 59 yards. He also came up with a huge end zone interception in the fourth quarter. When the Jags traded up to draft Hunter with the second overall pick in 2025, this is the kind of performance they were hoping to get on a regular basis, and Hunter now looks like he might be able to pull that off going forward. As for the rest of the team, this was an uncharacteristically bad performance by the defense, and once again, there were too many drops on offense. However, there's no reason for this team to be panicking about anything as they head into their Week 7 bye. Grade: B-As for the other grades that we've handed out so far in Week 6, you can check those out here. 
3. NFL Week 6 winners and losers: Giants and Rams had a rough Sunday
                                                                    Al Bello/Getty Images
                                                            You can't have a week of NFL action without having winners and losers, so here are some winners and losers. Carter Bahns came up with this week's list, and we're going to check out his losers below. LOSERS Giants. The situation in the Meadowlands is not a complete disaster, given that the Giants still lead the NFC East, but Sunday's loss hurts. There is no such thing as a "must-win" game in Week 6, but what the Giants just experienced was a defeat in a contest that held a lot of hope for New York. The opportunity to pull further ahead in a downtrodden division while playing a Saints team on a three-game losing streak escaped them. That result could haunt them down the line.Rams. The Rams, by way of tiebreakers, are the last-place team in the NFC West through Week 6. That is a sentence so difficult to fathom, considering their offseason successes, that it almost does not feel real. Anyone who has watched them play over the season's first month and a half understands why they hold a 2-4 record: They have looked nothing like the superstar-laden squad they are on paper. But that does not make it any easier to digest just how stunning a failure these first six weeks have been. Zachariah Branch's ball security. Rule No. 1 as a punt and kick returner is to hold onto the ball. Zachariah Branch failed to follow that rule in the Atlanta Falcons' 31-23 loss to the Chicago Bears. The rookie muffed a punt and fumbled during a kickoff return, and the Bears recovered both loose balls to help them build an overwhelming 31-7 lead.If you want to see Carter's list of winners (and a couple of other losers), be sure to click here.
    
    

    4. Overreactions from Week 6: Will the Rams make the playoffs? Everyone on the internet loves to overreact to things, and that's especially true when we're talking about the NFL. Personally, I overreact to everything. With that in mind, Zach Pereles decided to take a look at several things that happened during Week 6, so decide for yourself if we're all overreacting.  
Statement: The Rams won't make the playoffs playing like this.Overreaction or reality: Reality. This is simply a non-playoff team right now. The offense has very little juice, outside of an occasional excellent play by Puka Nacua or Davante Adams. It just feels really stagnant; Stafford used play action on 37% of his dropbacks last year and averaged 8.4 yards per pass on those throws. This year, it's down to 25% and 7.2, respectively. And when a team doesn't have juice, it has little room for error. But the Rams keep making errors: penalties, turnovers, missed assignments, etc. If they lose in Week 7, it's officially panic time.Statement: The Browns or Steelers will win the AFC North.Overreaction or reality: Overreaction. Cleveland technically leads the division thanks to Sunday's 13-10 win over Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore, and Pittsburgh is second because it has a better in-division record. Sorry, Browns and Steelers fans, but neither one of you is winning the division. Cleveland's largest win this season is by four points. It lost to the Jets just last week. Deshaun Watson looked awful Sunday. The Steelers looked similarly awful, needing a late comeback to force overtime against the Baker Mayfield-less Buccaneers. As it turns out, playing against backup quarterbacks is very helpful. Both teams rank in the bottom half of most major offensive stats. The quarterback play simply isn't good enough and won't be good enough, especially when put up against Lamar Jackson and Joe Burrow rather than Tyler Huntley and Jalon Daniels.Statement: Patriots made a mistake trading for A.J. Brown. Overreaction or reality: Overreaction. A.J. Brown's grand return from IR was ... not so grand. Three catches for 27 yards on 10 targets. Officially, he's been charged with two drops. Unofficially, given his high standards, it was probably more. He even bobbled away a Jets onside kick, but lucky for him, a teammate recovered to clinch the Patriots' 26-19 win. It's worth being concerned about the debut, but to say the trade is a bust or a mistake would be a drastic overreaction. Yes, it's been a tough start with the injury and the underwhelming return. But let's not write it off. Let's give him a week's worth of grace.
There are plenty more overreactions, and you can check them out here.5. 11 crazy stats from Week 6: Packers and Bills are defying history
                                                                    Michael Reaves/Getty Images
                                                            Every Sunday night, I get an email from our research department here at CBS Sports, and every Sunday, that email always includes some crazy stats about the games that were just played. With that in mind, here are 11 crazy stats from Week 6: Big game hunting. The Jaguars didn't win on Sunday, but Travis Hunter did have a huge game. The Jags' two-way player had a TD catch AND an interception, becoming the first player in 24 years to pull off both of those in the same game. The last player to accomplish that feat was Brian Dawkins in 2002. Bills defying history. NFL teams are 12-42 this season when giving up at least 30 points in a game, and that breaks down like this: The Bills are 4-0, while the other 31 teams are a combined 8-42. The Bills already have the second-most wins in a single season ever when giving up 30+, behind only the 2018 Rams, who won five games.  Packers defying history. In the 106-year history of the NFL, only three teams have ever had a winning record through six games without having a single player hit 50 yards rushing in any of those six games: 1935 Packers, 1941 Packers and 2026 Packers. Yup, the Packers are somehow the only team to do it, and they did it again this year. Patrick Mahomes tied Tom Brady in the record book. The Chiefs QB picked up his 100th career win on Sunday, and he did that in just his 131st career game. That ties him with Tom Brady for the record of fastest QB to reach 100 wins. Walking over the competition. With 128 yards against the Chargers, Kenneth Walker III now has an NFL-high 665 on the season.  That's the most rushing yards ever through five games by a player who's with a new team, topping a mark that was set by Eric Dickerson with the Rams in 1985. Comeback kids. The Steelers managed to beat the Buccaneers on Sunday despite trailing by 13 points in the fourth quarter. With the victory, they pulled off their largest comeback win since 2002. Germie Bernard also made some NFL history by becoming the first rookie with at least 10 receptions AND an overtime TD in the same game. Bear down. The return of Caleb Williams got all the headlines this week, but the Bears also got another player back (Kyler Gordon), and he ended up making NFL history. Gordon made his season debut on Sunday, and although he only played 16 snaps, that was enough time for him to rack up three sacks, along with forcing two fumbles. That makes him the first DB with at least three sacks and two forced fumbles in a game since 2000. Cardinals building a nest in Los Angeles. The Cardinals are 2-4 this season, and the twist is that both of their wins have come at SoFi Stadium. Not only did they beat the Rams on Sunday, but they also beat the Chargers in L.A. back in Week 1. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi (2) this year than the Rams and Chargers combined (1). McBride has been McAwesome. With seven catches for 53 yards against the Rams, McBride became the first player in NFL history with at least seven receptions in each of his team's first six games of the season. With 49 catches through six weeks, McBride also topped Zach Ertz's record (48) for the most catches by a tight end through the first six games. Alvin Kamara joins exclusive club. With 35 receiving yards against the Giants, Kamara now has 5,024 for his career. If you combine that with his 7,370 rushing yards, he's now just the sixth player in NFL history to have at least 5,000 rushing and 5,000 receiving yards in a career. Kamara joins Christian McCaffrey and Tiki Barber, along with Pro Football Hall of Famers Marcus Allen, Marshall Faulk and Lenny Moore. Old school Campbell. Calais Campbell had a sack against the Browns on Sunday, which is only notable because of his age. Since the sack became an official stat in 1982, Campbell is just the third player over the age of 40 to record a sack, joining Clay Matthews (6.5 sacks after turning 40) and Pro Football Hall of Famer Bruce Smith (five).If you see any other fun facts, feel free to tweet them at me. 
    
	

    6. Monday night preview: Picks and best bets for Commanders at 49ersThe 49ers (5-0) will be putting their undefeated record on the line against a Commanders (1-3-1) team that's looking to get its season turned around. The two head coaches in this game are extremely familiar with each other. Dan Quinn was the Falcons' head coach for six seasons (2015-20), and for two of those years, Kyle Shanahan was his offensive coordinator. They were coaching together in Super Bowl LI when the Falcons blew a 28-3 lead against the Patriots. So will anyone blow a 28-3 lead tonight? 
Here's one reason why each team should be feeling confident going into the game: Why the Commanders can win: If the Commanders have done one thing well this year, it's their ability to run the ball. This team is averaging 139.6 yards per game on the ground heading into Week 6, which is the sixth-most in the NFL. If the Commanders can run the ball, it will allow them to control the clock, keeping the 49ers and their high-powered offense off the field. The 49ers haven't really faced a mobile quarterback yet, so Jayden Daniels needs to keep San Francisco's defense on its toes by getting out of the pocket and making plays, and yup, he also needs to run. Under Dan Quinn, the Commanders are 11-3-1 when they rush for at least 150 yards, so if they can hit that magic number, that should give them a chance to pull off the upset. Why the 49ers can win: There's a reason the 49ers are undefeated: They're good at everything. Brock Purdy has the highest passer rating in the NFL for any QB who's started at least five games, and he leads the NFL in TD passes with 13. Not only can the 49ers beat you with the pass, but they also average 128.6 yards per game on the ground, which ranks in the top eight in the NFL. And now, this unstoppable offense gets to play a Commanders defense that has surrendered the third-most points per game (29.8) and the fourth-most passing yards per game (255) this year. The 49ers should be able to score on this defense, and if they hit 30, it's basically over. Since the start of the 2021 season, the 49ers are 38-1 when they score 30 points or more, including the playoffs. You can get a full preview of the game from Jared Dubin by clicking here.If you're thinking about betting on the game, here are a couple of props. ONE RECEIVING PROP I LIKE: George Kittle OVER 5.5 receptions (-102 at DraftKings): With Deebo Samuel out and Mike Evans banged up, Brock Purdy isn't going to have a lot of options Monday in the receiving game, so Kittle should see a solid share of targets. Kittle will be facing a Commanders defense that has given up the fourth-most passing yards this year. Also, opposing tight ends are averaging more than six catches per game against Washington. This seems like a solid matchup for Kittle.  ONE KICKING PROP I LIKE: Drew Stevens OVER 6.5 total points (-101 at DraftKings): The Commanders kicker has scored at least seven points in four straight games, and I feel like he can get to that number once again. Opposing teams are averaging 2.4 field goals per game against the 49ers, and if Stevens hits just two, then he'd need just one extra point to hit the over. I feel like this game will be a shootout, and that should include a lot of kicker points. If you're wondering how my props are doing this year, I'm 8-14 (3-8 on kicker props and 5-6 on all other props). After starting off 5-3, I'm now 3-11 on my last 14 props. That's clearly a sign that you should be fading me until further notice. And now, it's time for some picks. PICKS FOR 'MNF'Jared Dubin's pick:  49ers 27-16 over CommandersJordan Dajani's pick: 49ers 28-20 over CommandersJohn Breech's pick: 49ers 31-20 over CommandersTyler Sullivan's pick: 49ers 30-20 over CommandersPrisco's pick: 49ers 30-21 over Commanders
Over on our CBSSports.com picks page, all seven of us are taking the 49ers to win straight-up, and six of us are taking the 49ers to cover as a 7.5-point favorite.

title: MLB free agency: NPB star Teruaki Sato to be posted to MLB - CBS Sports
description: The lefty slugger could be a boon to several teams, and not just 2027 contenders
body:
The lefty slugger could be a boon to several teams, and not just 2027 contenders
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 19, 2026

            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Hanshin Tigers will post third baseman Teruaki Sato, Japan's Triple Crown winner this season, for MLB teams this offseason, the team announced on Monday. Sato, 28 in March, slugged 39 home runs with a .306/.383/.609 batting line in 2026. A year ago, he hit 40 home runs and was named league MVP, and it seems likely he will win MVP again this year.  "I am grateful to the team for respecting my wishes," Sato said in a statement, via Kyodo News.  This past March, Sato hit second for Japan in the World Baseball Classic and was the only non-MLB player in the top six of their lineup. Shohei Ohtani hit leadoff and Sato hit second, ahead of Seiya Suzuki, Masataka Yoshida, Kazuma Okamoto, and Munetaka Murakami, in that order. Sato went 3 for 10 in five WBC games.  
"He has been with us for six years, contributing to three league titles," Tigers GM Satoshi Shimamura said in a statement, via Kyodo News. "He delivered an especially outstanding performance this year."  
Given his age and power, and the weak MLB free agent class, Sato figures to be among the top targets for teams looking to add a bat this offseason. Murakami's two-year, $34 million contract with the Chicago White Sox has proven to be a bargain even with his second-half fade. Sato could command more than that despite being two years older than Murakami.  Here is what you need to know about Sato now that his availability to MLB teams has been made official.    What kind of player is he?  Obviously, Sato has power. His 39 home runs were one behind the league leader and came at a time when Japan is in something of a deadball era. The league hit .236/.301/.350 this year and averaged only 3.40 runs per game. For reference, MLB teams averaged 4.48 runs per game in 2026, and Myles Straw hit .241/.304/.342. Japan was an entire league of Myles Straws this season.  
Sato is a left-handed hitter and not quite Murakami 2.0. He doesn't have quite as much power, won't work as many walks, will still swing and miss a bunch, and likely isn't a third baseman long-term. Here is Just Baseball's scouting report from earlier this year:  From a tools standpoint, Sato's raw power may be as close to Murakami's as anyone out of Japan, and his in-zone contact rates are sturdier than his. The glaring weakness, however, is his chase rate. It has been stagnant since his sophomore season and still sits in the bottom third of NPB hitters ... That said, Sato does immense damage on pitches in his wheelhouse, and he swings the bat at a much higher overall rate than any of those players. The result is a profile built around elite power and above-average aggressiveness coupled with swing-and-miss concerns, perhaps closer in hitter archetype to someone like Cal Raleigh or Byron Buxton.  	 	MLB.com recently spoke to a scout who sees Sato as a corner outfielder or first baseman long-term, not a third baseman. Sato ran a 66% contact rate this season, below the 77% MLB average and in line with hitters like Brandon Lowe (67% in 2026) and Jake Burger (67%). Murakami ranked dead last among qualified hitters with a 60% contact rate in 2026.  Lowe is a reasonable offensive comp for Sato as a lefty hitter with 30-homer power and an OK walk rate. Whether Sato can stick at the hot corner is another matter. It only takes one MLB team to buy into him as a full-time third baseman, though Sato is seen as more athletic than Murakami, making the outfield a viable option. He's not necessarily destined for first base.  What are the posting rules?  Players from Japan can be posted as early as Nov. 1, and, once posted, they have 45 days to negotiate and sign a contract. The entire process (passing the physical, contract signing, etc.) must be complete within the 45 days. An agreement and a handshake isn't enough. If players do not sign within those 45 days, they return to Japan, though that's unlikely for Sato.  
The MLB team that signs Sato will have to pay the Tigers a posting fee that is based on the size of his contract. Here is the posting fee structure:  Contract valuePosting fee$25M or less 				 				20% of contract value 				 				$25M to $50M 				 				$5M plus 17.5% of contract value over $25M 				 				$50M or more 				 				$9.375M plus 15% of contract value over $50M 				 				For example, the White Sox paid Murakami's former team, the Yakult Swallows, a $6.575 million posting fee on his $34 million contract. That's $5 million on the first $25 million plus 17.5% of the remaining $9 million, which is $1.575 million. The $5 million plus $1.575 million equals the $6.575 million posting fee paid to the Swallows.  Barring a surprise agreement, the owners are expected to lock out the players when the collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1. The 45-day posting window was paused during the 2021 lockout, and the same strategy may be used this cycle. The Hiroshima Toyo Carp posted Suzuki on Nov. 21, 2021, his 45 days were paused when the lockout started on Dec. 1, then they resumed when the lockout ended on March 10, 2022. Suzuki signed with the Chicago Cubs on March 18.    Which MLB teams could be interested?  Sato is expected to draw significant interest this offseason and not just from contending teams. Murakami's success with the White Sox, a team that went 102 losses last season to the postseason this season, means even rebuilding clubs figure to pursue Sato. He's on the right side of 30 and brings hard-to-find power potential. Some possible landing spots:  
                            
    
                                                
                    
    New York Mets: It seems unlikely Bo Bichette will opt out, though the Mets have an opening at first base and could also rotate Sato through the DH spot. Jorge Polanco is still under contract next season and Jared Young showed enough this year to get at-bats next year, which could perhaps steer the Mets away from Sato. Bichette opting out would change things.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
    New York Yankees: The Yankees received some of the worst third base production in the game in 2026 and are expected to replace incumbent Ryan McMahon this winter. They are overstuffed with first basemen (Luis García Jr., Ben Rice) and DHs (Rice, Giancarlo Stanton), so they would have to believe in Sato's ability to play the hot corner to pursue him seriously.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Philadelphia Phillies: The Phillies must replace free agent-to-be Alec Bohm at third base and they need an outfielder badly. Sato could be a fit at either position, and if push comes to shove, they can always put Bryce Harper back in the outfield and slot Sato in at first base. The only downside would be adding another lefty bat to an offense that is already heavy on lefties.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
    St. Louis Cardinals: St. Louis is open to adding a short-term third baseman as they wait for top prospect Jesús Báez, who slugged 25 home runs in only 59 Double-A games in 2026. Sato on a short-term contract may not be doable, but it's worth making the call. The Cardinals are a team on the upswing and the 27-year-old would fit in nicely with the rest of their core.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Washington Nationals: Washington is an arrow-up organization with the flexibility to slot Sato in at first base, third base, the corner outfield, or DH. His age lines up with their core well. Just about the only downside is adding another lefty bat to a lineup that is already heavy on lefties, but that's not a dealbreaker. The Nationals and Sato are an excellent match on paper.

title: AP Top 25 poll reactions: Michigan overrated; Kansas, UK underrated in preseason college basketball rankings - CBS Sports
description: Here are teams ranked too high or too low in the first AP Top 25 poll before the 2026-27 season
body:
Here are teams ranked too high or too low in the first AP Top 25 poll before the 2026-27 season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 19, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:38 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The AP Top 25 men's basketball poll was released Monday, another signal that the start of the 2026-27 college basketball season is around the corner. Unsurprisingly, Florida earned the No. 1 spot in the poll after receiving 47 of 59 possible first-place votes. The Gators are the favorites to win the 2027 national title after returning four starters from a team that earned a No. 1 seed in the NCAA Tournament last season.Duke, Illinois, UConn and Arizona rounded out the top five of the preseason rankings. This year's Top 25 poll was significantly harder to fill out than in previous seasons, as many teams are still awaiting word on whether one or more of their players will be granted a fifth year of eligibility. For Kansas, news dropped just hours before the first poll of the season, revealing that former Purdue star Trey Kaufman-Renn would be joining the program.
        
            
                College basketball rankings: Florida earns No. 1 spot in preseason AP Top 25 poll ahead of Duke, Illinois
                
                    Cameron Salerno                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Kaufman-Renn is hoping to be granted a sixth year of eligibility to play during the 2026-27 season. His new teammates at Kansas -- Melvin Council Jr. and Tre White -- are seeking a fifth year of eligibility. If all three players are cleared, the Jayhawks are a top 10 team in the sport.
With the first AP poll of the season out, let's dive into the overrated and underrated teams, which are headlined by the reigning national champions and Kansas.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Overrated: MichiganAP Top 25 ranking: No. 16In our AP poll predictions, I had Michigan slotted at No. 17. Heading into the season, Michigan's roster is somewhere in the 20s. Last season, I predicted Michigan to win the Big Ten because of the talent on the roster and how good a coach Dusty May is/was at the college level.With May now off to the NBA, and questions about the roster looming -- in part because of Brandon McCoy Jr. being out of the season and the eligibility status of Roddy Gayle Jr. in question -- I'm expecting Michigan to take a step back this season. Even if Gayle is ruled eligible, Michigan will finish behind USC and UCLA -- two teams ranked behind them in the poll -- in the final Big Ten standings.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Underrated: KansasAP Top 25 ranking: No. 17News broke quite literally hours before the AP poll came out that Kaufman-Renn would be joining Kansas' roster. There are still major questions about whether TKR will ultimately be ruled eligible to play, but on paper (as of today!), Kansas is a top 10 team.A frontcourt of Kaufman-Renn and Tyran Stokes is very intriguing. Add that duo with White, Council, and five-star guard Taylen Kinney, and you have a roster that is better on paper than last season, which featured five-star guard Darryn Peterson, the No. 2 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft. Retirement questions have been looming around Bill Self for the last few years, so it makes sense for the Jayhawks to go all-in to at least try and get Kaufman-Renn eligible. Self deserves one final run before calling it a career on his terms.
        
            
                Trey Kaufman-Renn signs with Kansas: Former Purdue star is seeking unprecedented sixth year of eligibility
                
                    Cameron Salerno                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Overrated: VirginiaAP Top 25 ranking: No. 9The one team within the top 10 that is overrated is the Virginia Cavaliers. In our preseason predictions, I had the Cavaliers projected to slot No. 10 in the first poll of the season, which wasn't far off from what the voters thought.
I wrote this in our ACC preseason prediction post, but Virginia is the fourth-best team in the ACC behind Duke, Miami and Louisville. If I had a ballot to fill out, I would've slotted Miami somewhere in the 8-10 range and Louisville not far behind, with Virginia landing somewhere in the early teens.
        
            
                ACC expert picks: 2026-27 projected order of finish, preseason predictions, top players to watch
                
                    Cameron Salerno                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Underrated: KentuckyAP Top 25 ranking: No. 23Where Kentucky was slotted in the AP poll was something I was keeping a close eye on. I had Kentucky projected to be ranked No. 21 in our predictions, which isn't far off from what voters did.After being arguably the most disappointing team in college basketball that underachieved with a high-priced roster, this will be a bounce-back year for Mark Pope and company. The addition of former Iowa State star Milan Momcilovic and the potential Year 2 jump from Malachi Moreno will make Kentucky "underrated" in a loaded SEC this season. The key storyline to monitor is how Alex Wilkins and Zoom Diallo operate in the backcourt. CBS Sports' Matt Norlander reported that Wilkins will be the point guard running the transition offense, while junior point guard Diallo will run the sets in the halfcourt. If it works, it will pay off big time.

        
            
                SEC Media Days Takeaways: Florida's Rueben Chinyelu guarantees national title, LSU litigation saga continues
                
                    Matt Norlander                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Underrated: MiamiAP Top 25 ranking: No. 14Miami is the team I thought would land in the top 10 of the preseason AP poll. Instead, the Hurricanes will begin the season ranked No. 14, with a chance to improve their ranking significantly during the opening week if they can upset in-state foe Florida.Miami is the second-best team in the ACC. The fact that they're slotted below Louisville and Virginia is surprising. However, that projection also hinges on whether Malik Reneau, Miami's leading scorer from last season, is granted a fifth year. Even if he isn't, getting back Shelton Henderson and adding Acaden Lewis and Somto Cyril via the transfer portal makes this roster better than last season.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Underrated: Texas TechAP Top 25 ranking: No. 19If you told me today that Donovan Atwell, Darrion Williams and Jamichael Stillwell will all be granted a fifth year of eligibility, I would comfortably have Texas Tech as a top 10 team in college basketball. While it's not surprising that Texas Tech is ranked this low (they were No. 23 in our projections for that reason alone), this is a team that can win the Big 12 at full strength.
Williams played a significant role in Texas Tech reaching the Elite Eight and being minutes away from knocking off eventual national champion Florida in 2025. Atwell is one of the best shooters in college basketball. Momcilovic is the only returner in the sport who knocked down more 3-pointers last season. And you can't forget about JT Toppin, who is working his way back from a torn ACL suffered late last season. When Toppin is healthy, he is arguably the best player in college basketball. Texas Tech will significantly outperform its preseason ranking if everyone is eligible.

title: Bold predictions for 2026-27 NBA season: Victor Wembanyama double dips, a Knicks letdown, huge trades, more - CBS Sports
